accepted.question_text: For the integral form of a Jack superpolynomial in superspace, defined by J^(alpha)_Lambda = sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega, is every expansion coefficient v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) always a polynomial in alpha with integer coefficients?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 - [14] The coefficients vLambdaOmega(alpha) are polynomials in alpha with integer coefficients, that is, they belong to Z[alpha].

accepted.question_text: Is there a combinatorial description, analogous to the one known in the ordinary Jack-polynomial setting, for the coefficients v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) appearing in the monomial expansion J^(alpha)_Lambda = sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega of integral-form Jack superpolynomials?

evidence.quote: Open problem 3.2 - Find a combinatorial description, analogous to that of [31], for the expansion coefficients vLambdaOmega(alpha) in (3.39).

accepted.question_text: Fix k >= 1 and N. For the space F_N^(k) of symmetric superpolynomials in N even variables and N odd variables that vanish whenever x_1 = x_2 = ... = x_{k+1}, do the Jack superpolynomials P^(alpha_{k,2})_Lambda(x_1, ..., x_N, theta_1, ..., theta_N) indexed by (k, 2, N)-admissible superpartitions form a basis of F_N^(k)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3 - The Jack superpolynomials P^(alpha_{k,2})_Lambda(x1, . . . , xN, theta1, . . . , thetaN), with Lambda (k, 2, N)-admissible, form a basis of the space F_N^(k).

accepted.question_text: What is the precise connection between admissible superpartitions, the associated Jack superpolynomials in superspace, and the basis states of irreducible Neveu-Schwarz modules in the minimal superconformal model M(2, 4p)?

evidence.quote: Open problem 3.4 - Connection with superconformal field theory. The basis of states for the irreducible Neveu-Schwarz modules in minimal superconformal model M(2, 4p) can be characterized by admissible superpartitions [34].

accepted.question_text: For Macdonald superpolynomials in superspace, does the automorphism rho_{q,t} satisfy the second duality relation rho_{q,t}(P_Lambda(q, t)) = t^{|Lambda'a|} Q_{Lambda'}(t, q) for every superpartition Lambda?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1 - From the action of rho_{q,t}, we have the (second) duality relation rho_{q,t}(P_Lambda(q, t)) = t^{|Lambda'a|} Q_{Lambda'}(t, q).

accepted.question_text: For any two superpartitions Lambda and Omega of the same degree, does the normalized Macdonald superpolynomial satisfy the symmetry identity P_tilde_Lambda(u_Omega) = P_tilde_Omega(u_Lambda), where u_Lambda denotes the specialization determined by Lambda?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 - (Symmetry). [41] For any superpartitions Lambda, Omega of the same degree, we have P_tilde_Lambda(u_Omega) = P_tilde_Omega(u_Lambda).

accepted.question_text: When the modified Macdonald superpolynomial H_Lambda(q, t) is expanded in the Schur superpolynomial basis as H_Lambda(q, t) = sum_Omega K_{Omega,Lambda}(q, t) s_Omega, are all coefficients K_{Omega,Lambda}(q, t) polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 - (Positivity). [23] The coefficients KOmegaLambda(q, t) are, for all superpartitions Lambda and Omega, polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients, that is, they belong to N[q, t].

accepted.question_text: Can one obtain explicit Littlewood-Richardson rules in superspace for the coefficients c^Gamma_{Lambda,Omega} and cbar^Gamma_{Lambda,Omega} that govern products of Schur superpolynomials and their dual variants?

evidence.quote: Open problem 6.7 - An interesting problem would be to obtain Littlewood-Richardson rules for the coefficients c^Gamma_{LambdaOmega}, cbar^Gamma_{LambdaOmega}.

accepted.question_text: For the ideal I_N^(k,r) spanned by Jack superpolynomials indexed by (k, r, N)-admissible superpartitions, is the inclusion I_N^(k,r) subseteq F_N^(k) actually an equality when r = 2?
accepted.context_brief: Equality of admissible Jack ideal and vanishing space

evidence.quote: In addition, we conjecture that the inclusion in the last result is in fact an equality when r = 2.
